label: late copy-phase step whose input is w/b/m/t/g
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (never during the original inputs or at <DEL>), and only on the fed-back copy of an earlier token (in_first is always 0). Activity is concentrated at the end of the sequence: 57% of mass is on the final step (to_go=0) and 27% on the step before it. Rate rises steeply with recall_idx (17x lift at recall_idx 8), so long sequences (L=9) dominate. The input token matters a lot: w, b, m, t, g carry about 94% of mass. w and b give the largest activations (top examples are mostly b/w/m at the last or second-to-last step). Other inputs such as vowels, s and q almost never fire it. This envelope is necessary but far from sufficient: only about 11% of qualifying steps are active on dev, and conditioning on in_count, prev_tok or out_tok did not give a clean rule, so whatever else decides firing is not captured here. Overall it is a sparse neuron (about 0.26% of steps).

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=w (+6.07), phase=2 & in_tok=b (+5.59), phase=2 & in_tok=m (+5.03), phase=2 & in_tok=t (+4.59), phase=2 & in_tok=g (+4.24), phase=2 & in_tok=0 (+3.06). Lower it: out_tok=q (-2.38), prev_tok=<DEL> (-2.34), recall_idx=1 (-2.34), out_tok=- (-2.14).
